gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-kufi-arabic: Quilon is an editorial display face whose strokes swell and thin with a gentle, pencil-sharp restraint. Noto Kufi Arabic is the sans-serif underneath, modern and open, and a full page of it would read smoothly, with capitals barely taller than the lowercase.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans: Quilon speaks with editorial authority and moderate shading. Its heading shapes carry the drama with tall, generous openings, while Noto Sans does the quieter job of filling lines with lowercase that takes up most of the height.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Noto Sans Adlam has curve endings kept well apart and a tall, full c, s and z, which makes it a friendly body face. Quilon sits above with a gentle modulation, and a generous heading size would let that commanding editorial voice come through.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-adlam-unjoine: Quilon leads with commanding editorial strokes, its thins about half the weight of its thicks. Noto Sans Adlam Unjoined follows in a modern sans-serif with generous gaps where curves meet stems and little difference between cases, so paragraphs of it move along without any fuss.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-anatolian-hie: Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs has terminal tips pointing outward and an x-height rising close to the cap height, giving the body a modern look. Quilon above it swells and tapers along its curves, while Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs keeps extended reading brisk and uncluttered.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-arabic: Quilon brings editorial command, its thicks and thins kept in moderation. Noto Sans Arabic carries on below with wide openings and a pronounced x-height, so a long stretch of text stays clean and easy on the eye.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Approachable and tidy, with a tall, full c, s and z. Noto Sans Armenian keeps its round letters wide and inviting beneath Quilon, whose slight pinch where curves meet stems adds an editorial edge, so long paragraphs read comfortably.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-avestan: Sharp editorial headings, with stroke weights differing just enough to feel alive, over a clean modern body. Noto Sans Avestan, with its tall x-height and curve tips that never touch, lets Quilon do the talking.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Commanding up top, Quilon has the mild stroke variation of a dip pen used gently, and an editorial confidence to match. And Noto Sans Bamum answers underneath with big open counters in every small letter, a modern sans that keeps the page legible.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-bassa-vah: Quilon opens with editorial command and medium contrast in its strokes, a display face with real presence. Noto Sans Bassa Vah follows in a professional sans, its dominant midsection and open-jawed c making a long page feel full and easy to follow.
